current_pack_decisions.rationale: The mandatory foundation is used by every scenario and its evidence, citation, critical-thinking, and onboarding responsibilities form one trust boundary.
current_pack_decisions.target_boundary: Retain as the mandatory baseline and do not add domain or workflow procedures.

current_pack_decisions.rationale: The full-cycle route uses the complete pack, but literature-only and publication-only routes install hypothesis generation and study design without needing them.
current_pack_decisions.target_boundary: Create research-design and literature-publication packs; retain the current ID only as a compatibility aggregate for full-cycle selection.

current_pack_decisions.rationale: PDF-only work installs database retrieval and exploratory analysis, while dataset-only work installs document conversion; the procedures have separate user triggers.
current_pack_decisions.target_boundary: Create document-evidence and structured-data-analysis packs with the current ID retained only as a compatibility aggregate.

current_pack_decisions.rationale: Statistics, power, units, uncertainty, and scientific visualization share assumptions and review checks; the main over-installation comes from broad domain selection, not the skill boundary.
current_pack_decisions.target_boundary: Keep one quantitative pack but tighten selection when a domain alone is the only quantitative signal.

prioritized_additions.cross_taxonomy_reason: A recurring workflow needs scheduled retrieval, deduplication, state, and source-linked digest behavior across multiple disciplines.
Eligibility criteria, reproducible search, screening decisions, and deduplication form a workflow absent from conventional literature review.
Codebooks, traceable coding, reflexivity, and thematic synthesis are shared methods used in both social science and humanities routes.
Image provenance, transformations, measurements, and interpretation checks are material-specific procedures spanning engineering and life sciences.
Protocol, bias, safety, and reporting checks require domain evidence beyond generic study design and must pass independent expert review.
